transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Well, I'm here because... it's about driving. Specifically, driving over bridges. What finally made me come in is that the moment my car reaches one of those long bridges toward Miami, my chest just tightens up. My hands clamp down on the steering wheel, and I get this sudden, overwhelming certainty that I have to get off right away... even though there's nowhere to go once you're on it.
Do these intense episodes ever happen when you’re not on a bridge?
No, not really. If I'm just driving on regular roads or... running errands around town, I feel perfectly fine. It's really just the bridges. I don't get that feeling anywhere else.
When you’re on a bridge, is the main fear the height?

I'm not really sure if it's the height, to be honest. I haven't really thought about it quite like that. It's more just... the bridge itself, I think. Just being out there and knowing I can't pull over or get off. So, no, I wouldn't say how high up I am is the main thing I'm focusing on.
When you’re on a bridge, is the scariest part feeling trapped because you can’t get off?

I'm not entirely sure if that's it. I mean... I haven't really tried to pinpoint what the absolute scariest part is. It all just sort of hits me at once, and I just know I don't want to be there. So I really couldn't say for sure if feeling trapped is the main thing.
If that same road were at ground level instead of on a bridge, would it still feel just as scary?
No, I don't think so. If it's just a regular road on the ground, I'm fine. It's really just the fact that it's a bridge that bothers me.
When you're on a bridge, are you afraid of being high above the ground or water?

Well, no, I wouldn't say it's that either. I don't really think about what's underneath the bridge, whether it's water or a valley or whatever. It's just... being on the structure itself that gets to me. I don't really look down and worry about what's below.
When you’re on a bridge, are you afraid it might collapse or that you might fall off it?

No, I can't say that's it either. I know they're built well enough, so I don't sit there thinking the whole thing is going to break apart. And I'm usually just sitting inside a car, so I'm not worried about tumbling over the edge. It's just... well, it's just a terrible feeling of being on it, without any specific thought like that.
Would crossing a long bridge over water feel more frightening to you than crossing a bridge over land?

No, I don't think it makes a difference. Water or land... it's really all the same to me. Like I was saying a minute ago, I don't pay much attention to what's underneath. A bridge is a bridge, and just being on one is what causes that terrible feeling, no matter what it happens to be crossing over.
Are bridges especially frightening to you because they go over water?

Well, like I just mentioned a moment ago, no, the water doesn't really have anything to do with it. It doesn't matter to me if there's a river down there or just dry land. It's purely the bridge itself that I can't handle.
Do you feel the same kind of fear when you’re up high in other places, like on a balcony or near the edge of a tall building?
No, I really don't. Being on a balcony or looking out a window from a high floor doesn't bother me at all. I don't have a general fear of heights. It's... it's just bridges. Only bridges.
If you had to walk across a pedestrian bridge, would that feel just as frightening to you?

Yes, I'm sure it would. Like I said, a bridge is a bridge. Whether I'm in a car or... well, walking across one on foot, the feeling is exactly the same. I just wouldn't do it. The fear is just as strong because I'm still on a bridge, and that's the part I can't handle.
